name: Huli Huli Chicken — Hawaiian Grilled Chicken with Pineapple-Shoyu Glaze
subtitle: Hawaiian Grilled Chicken with Pineapple-Shoyu Glaze
description: The roadside fundraiser classic: chicken marinated in shoyu, pineapple juice, brown sugar, ketchup and ginger, grilled and turned ("huli" means turn) while basted with the reduced glaze. Serves 6.

ingredients.text: 1.6 kg bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks
ingredients.item: bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks

steps.text: Whisk 240 ml pineapple juice, 120 ml shoyu (soy sauce), 110 g brown sugar, 80 ml ketchup, 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 2 tbsp grated ginger, 4 garlic cloves, grated and 1 tsp sriracha (optional). Set aside 250 ml for the glaze.
Put 1.6 kg bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks in a zip bag with the rest of the marinade and refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight.
Simmer the reserved sauce in a small pan for 10 minutes, until reduced by about half and syrupy.

Set up a grill for two-zone cooking (one side hot, one side off) and oil the grates with 1 tbsp neutral oil (for the grill). Grill the chicken skin side up over indirect heat, lid closed, for 30 minutes, turning once.
Move the chicken over direct heat and grill 8 minutes, turning every 2 minutes and brushing with the glaze each time, until lacquered, charred in spots and 80°C at the bone.
Rest 5 minutes, brush with the last of the glaze and scatter with 3 scallions, sliced. Serve with rice and mac salad.

notes:
The sugar in the marinade burns over direct heat, which is why the chicken cooks through on the cool side first and only gets glazed at the end. Oven method: bake at 200°C for 35 minutes, then broil 5 minutes, brushing with glaze every 2 minutes.

Boneless thighs work too: grill 5 minutes per side over medium-direct heat, then glaze. Mesquite or kiawe wood chips get closer to the roadside flavor.
